figures.depicts: Color photograph outside a hospital 'EMERGENCY Adult & Pediatric Trauma Center' ambulance entrance: two uniformed EMS providers, a nurse in a gown, a physician in a white coat, and another provider in masks standing together; a wheeled stretcher at the left edge and a 'STOP — TRIAGE NOW IN TENT' easel sign at the right. A scene photo of the emergency care team where EMS hands off to the hospital; no labels or instructional content.

cards.why: the caption names the continuum of care and the photo shows the unified team at the first-contact-to-hospital seam the card defines; congruent illustration (overshoot doctrine), nothing on it leaks an answer

figures.depicts: Pennsylvania Department of Health '4-Person Pit Crew CPR Example (2 BLS and 2 ALS)' training diagram: a red triangle around a supine patient with four provider silhouettes, and four text boxes assigning each position's tasks — Position 1 (BLS) assess patient and start CPR, alternate 100 compressions; Position 2 (BLS) attach monitor/defibrillator pads, alternate compressions, ventilate; Position 3 (ALS) airway, oxygen, rhythm check/shock, capnography; Position 4 (ALS Team Leader) IO/IV, epinephrine, amiodarone, treatable causes, CPR checklist — plus a key and protocol notes.

cards.why: the plate depicts role assignments by position — the clear-roles element, not the shared-goal element this card tests; same-topic, different-subject (the FIGURE 4-2 class)
the card's Ex line is pit crew CPR defining each intervention and role in advance; the plate depicts exactly that, position by position, on the back

figures.depicts: Color photograph of two EMS providers in high-visibility vests and masks standing beside an ambulance; the left one holds a portable radio and raises one gloved hand in a signal. A generic crew-collaboration scene photo; no labels, no depicted technique or content.

cards.why: a scene photo; depicts no plan-alteration broadcast — a viewer asks why the picture is there
depicts no leadership content; merely near the team-leader passage (R19 nearby-not-about)
depicts neither Alert nor Emergency routing; generic crew photo
depicts none of the four communication elements; generic crew photo
depicts no closed-loop exchange a viewer could see; generic crew photo
depicts no PACE content; generic crew photo

figures.depicts: Vertical five-box flowchart on a blue-gray ground, downward arrows between boxes: Gather data -> Interpret the data -> Develop a plan -> Communicate and implement the plan -> Evaluate the outcome.

cards.why: the plate IS the card's five-step sequence; rule 26's attach-the-procedure's-plate mandate, back side so the whole loop is visible after answering
